chapter: Swing and what makes a band play
title: Does the band swing every night, and why hungry bands play best
summary: He says his band had to swing every night, and that bands play best when they come off the road hungry rather than after a big meal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, the only thing I'm going to say is this, now. Let's say you -- when you have let's say a Tadd Dameron arrangement, a fairly heavily written piece. Now one night you're going to swing it and one night you're not, right?
You say now speaking of like a Tadd Dameron arrangement?
Well, supposing you get a fairly
heavy arrangement and you're not going to -- your band is going to play it every night, but one night it swings and one night it doesn't. Is that possible?
No.
It's going to swing every night?
They got to swing.
Every night.
See, that (inaudible).
In other words, we going to find out what's wrong if it didn't swing.
Yeah.
We have to find out what went wrong.
But I mean there is the element of one night you feel good and one night you don't.

Well, now, that happens in all groups. Now, say for instance, now you can take a band and feed a band, have a great dinner for them and this and that and the other and 30 minutes, 45 minutes to an hour, they got to go on the stand. They ain't going to do nothing. They're not going to do nothing because they're on a full stomach. They can't get together.
They're logey.
They can't coordinate.
On a full stomach?
That's right. One is a little fuller
than the other, one is fuller than the other, this one is this full and this one is overstuffed, blab, blab, and that's what you've got happening.

Now if you want to hear a band play, you catch a band that just got in off the road, just got in town, haven't had a chance to get anything to eat, they haven't eaten a thing, but they got to go right on the bandstand and play. They play.
Why is that?
They coordinate better. The everything better.
Well, Stan, let me say something. You know, you feed them up and you get logey, you know?
Yeah, yeah.
You lose the sharpness, you're dull.
They lose it.
No, I just wanted to -- I can understand that, too, but I wanted to see what Jay would say, you know.

The best that I ever heard the big band play was under those conditions. The best I ever heard them play. And I can almost remember the night especially -- the particular nights, you know what I mean, because I would get up from the piano and I'd say, "I'm going to get up and walk away and just listen for -- listen at this tune." And I'd
get up and walk away and listen at it. And that was those hungry nights.
(Laughter.)
Very funny, isn't it, really?
It's a funny thing, but it is true. They play far better, more superior and everything.
